extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, regulators, environmental lawyers, and public interest commenters engaged in notice-and-comment and administrative litigation
extracted.subtask_description: Legal public-comment submission analyzing whether an agency technical report (the Draft CWG Report) complies with federal information quality, peer review, FACA, and scientific-integrity requirements and explaining why reliance on the report would be arbitrary and capricious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information must be presented in an accurate, clear, complete and unbiased manner
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE IQA Guidelines: disseminated information should be 'presented in an accurate, clear, complete and unbiased manner' and as a matter of substance must be 'accurate, reliable, and unbiased.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to agency reports: conclusions and framing must not be misleading or incomplete; pervasive errors or misrepresentations violate objectivity standards. Anti-patterns include selective framing, omission of contrary evidence, or presentation that obscures prevailing scientific consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific data and analysis must use sound statistical and research methods
rubrics_metrics.description: In a 'scientific ... context' the original and supporting data should be generated, and the analytical results developed, using sound statistical and research methods (DOE IQA Guidelines at 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency scientific products must document data generation and analytic methods consistent with accepted standards; failures in methodology or undocumented analyses undermine objectivity and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of objectivity through formal, independent, external peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE IQA Guidelines (and OMB) state that if information has been subjected to 'formal, independent, external peer review,' it 'may generally be presumed to be of acceptable objectivity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a work product has not undergone formal independent external peer review, it is not entitled to that presumption; absence of peer review is a substantial defect for influential scientific information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with OMB Final Information Quality Bulletin for Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: All information disseminated to the public must comply with OMB’s Final Information Quality Bulletin for Peer Review (DOE IQA Guidelines at 8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency reports that inform significant policy decisions must meet OMB peer-review requirements (e.g., documentation, transparency about reviewers/procedures); failure to do so is a violation of agency IQA obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influential information is subject to heightened quality and transparency standards
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB defines influential information as 'scientific information the agency reasonably can determine will have or does have a clear and substantial impact on important public policies or private sector decisions.' DOE’s definition includes 'information on which a regulatory action with a $100 million per year impact is based.' (DOE IQA Guidelines at 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information qualifying as 'influential' (or DOE's $100M threshold) must meet higher standards of quality, transparency, and documentation; agencies must take 'extra care' to ensure highest quality when information is influential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure scientific integrity: involve scientists with appropriate expertise and avoid misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA Scientific Integrity Policy: decisionmakers should involve scientists with appropriate expertise; scientific information and processes must manifest scientific integrity, quality, rigor, and objectivity; ensure studies used undergo appropriate independent peer review and do not 'knowingly misrepresent, exaggerate, or downplay areas of scientific uncertainty.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must select experts with relevant expertise, subject science to independent review, and accurately represent uncertainties. Anti-patterns include selecting non-experts or intentionally misrepresenting uncertainty to support predetermined policy goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISI/HISA work products should undergo peer review; HISA requires rigorous external review
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA Peer Review Handbook: work products designated as ISI (Influential Scientific Information) or HISA (Highly Influential Scientific Assessment) 'should be peer reviewed.' ISI is work that 'will have or does have a clear and substantial impact on important public policies or private sector decisions.' HISA is ISI that could have >$500 million impact in any year or is novel, controversial, precedent-setting, or has significant interagency interest. HISAs 'are expected to undergo rigorous external peer review with opportunities for public participation,' with external panels preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an agency product meets ISI/HISA criteria (e.g., establishes precedent, affects economy, addresses controversial issues, has interagency implications), it should receive rigorous external peer review and public participation. Failure to do so is inconsistent with EPA practice and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate information quality principles at every development step; external peer review is 'procedure of choice' for important decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA Guidelines for Ensuring and Maximizing the Quality... state that principles of information quality should be integrated into each step of development, including creation, collection, maintenance, and dissemination; external peer review is the 'procedure of choice' for work products 'intended to support the most important decisions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should build quality, documentation, and review into each phase of producing scientific information; for major policy decisions, external peer review is expected. Anti-patterns include creating a report in secrecy and releasing it only to coincide with rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a 'weight-of-evidence' approach and give greater weight to peer-reviewed studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines recommend a 'weight-of-evidence' approach: 'a well-developed, peer-reviewed study would generally be accorded greater weight than information from a less well-developed study that had not been peer-reviewed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple studies exist, agencies must consider the totality of evidence and explicitly reconcile inconsistencies, favoring robust peer-reviewed work. Failure to weigh evidence (or disproportionately weighting non-peer-reviewed work) undermines decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: When disseminating influential scientific information ensure accuracy, reliability, unbiasedness, and use best available science
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will ensure, to the extent practicable, that influential scientific information regarding human health, safety or environmental risk assessments is 'accurate, reliable and unbiased,' using 'the best available science and supporting studies conducted in accordance with sound and objective scientific practices, including, when available, peer reviewed science and supporting studies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must document reliance on best available science, cite peer-reviewed studies that support or contradict estimates of risk, and explain methodologies used to reconcile inconsistencies. Omission of such documentation is a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Assessment Factor — Soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness: '[t]he extent to which the scientific and technical procedures, measures, methods or models employed to generate the information are reasonable for, and consistent with, the intended application.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether methods are consistent with accepted scientific theory or approaches; check for independent verification. Anti-pattern: use of unreasonable methods or unvalidated models for intended application.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Assessment Factor — Applicability and Utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability and utility: '[t]he extent to which the information is relevant for the Agency’s intended use.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the information directly supports the regulatory decision or is tangential; irrelevant or misapplied information should be given less or no weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Assessment Factor — Clarity and Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity and completeness: '[t]he degree of clarity and completeness with which the data, assumptions, methods, quality assurance, sponsoring organizations and analyses employed to generate the information are documented.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require full documentation of data, assumptions, methods, QA; undocumented analyses or hidden assumptions reduce credibility and violate guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Assessment Factor — Uncertainty and Variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncertainty and variability: '[t]he extent to which the variability and uncertainty (quantitative and qualitative) in the information or in the procedures, measures, methods or models are evaluated and characterized.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must quantify and qualitatively describe uncertainty and variability and not obscure or downplay them. Anti-patterns include claiming certainty where substantial uncertainty exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Assessment Factor — Evaluation and Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation and review: '[t]he extent of independent verification, validation and peer review of the information or of the procedures, measures, methods or models.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether independent verification/validation/peer review occurred; lack of independent review is a critical deficiency for high-stakes information.

rubrics_metrics.name: FACA formation requirements: consult GSA, publish Federal Register notice, and file a charter before forming
rubrics_metrics.description: FACA implementing regulations require agencies to consult with GSA's Committee Management Secretariat and, once that review is complete, publish a notice announcing establishment in the Federal Register before forming a new advisory committee; every advisory committee must file a charter before it meets or takes any action (5 U.S.C. § 1008; 41 C.F.R. § 102-3.60).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow pre-formation procedural steps; forming a committee in secret without consultation, notice, or charter violates FACA and renders actions unlawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: FACA fair-balance membership requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: FACA requires committee membership be 'fairly balanced in terms of the points of view represented and the functions to be performed by the advisory committee' and that agencies 'make appropriate provisions to assure that the advice and recommendations ... will not be inappropriately influenced by the appointing authority or by any special interest.' (5 U.S.C. § 1004(b)(2)-(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must prepare a Membership Balance Plan describing targeted points of view, selection criteria, and outreach; failure to assemble a fairly balanced committee (e.g., hand-picking only skeptics) violates FACA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership Balance Plan and outreach obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must submit a 'Membership Balance Plan' describing how to attain fairly balanced membership, including the points of view to be represented, intended selection criteria and outreach efforts; the plan must be uploaded to the FACA database when filing the charter (41 C.F.R. § 102-3.60(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must conduct broad outreach using varied methods to reach stakeholders and document outreach in the plan; failure to conduct outreach or file the plan is a procedural violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE advisory committee procedural requirements (Action Memorandum, member attributes matrix)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE Manual requires the proposal package for a new advisory committee include an 'Action Memorandum' with a description of the plan for ensuring fairly balanced committee membership and a matrix/table presenting members' attributes (e.g., geographic location; residential or commercial consumer) to demonstrate balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE-specific administrative steps (Action Memorandum, member attribute matrix) must be completed; omission demonstrates failure to follow agency-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: FACA meeting openness and records-disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: With limited exceptions, all 'meetings' of advisory committee members must be open to the public, noticed in the Federal Register, and the public must be able to attend, appear before, and file statements with the committee; all 'records, reports, transcripts, minutes, appendixes, working papers, drafts, studies, agenda, or other documents' made available to or prepared for or by each advisory committee must be available to the public, with only limited exceptions; agencies must ensure 'contemporaneous availability of advisory committee records' (5 U.S.C. §§ 1009, 1007; 41 C.F.R. §§ 102-3.150, 102-3.170).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency obligations require contemporaneous disclosure of meetings and records; intentionally concealing meetings/records or delaying release to limit public participation violates FACA and associated regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory committee experts must be appointed as Special Government Employees (SGEs) and comply with ethics/conflict-of-interest rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For DOE-established advisory committees, members serving as experts must be appointed as SGEs. Under federal law SGEs may not 'participate[] personally and substantially ... in any particular matter in which, to his knowledge, ... he ... has a financial interest.' (18 U.S.C. § 208). DOE Manual also requires disclosure of financial and other interests prior to becoming advisory committee members and prohibits participation in matters with direct predictable impact on organizations with which they are associated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure advisors are properly appointed, disclose conflicts, and are screened from participation in particular matters where disqualifying financial interests exist. Failure to appoint SGEs or obtain disclosures risks ethical violations and invalidates committee actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify peer-reviewed studies and reconcile inconsistencies when supporting risk estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA Guidelines require agencies to 'specify peer-reviewed studies known to the Administrator that support, are directly relevant to, or fail to support any estimate of risk and the methodology used to reconcile inconsistencies in the scientific data.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an agency cites studies to support risk estimates, it must list supporting and contradictory peer-reviewed work and explain how inconsistencies were reconciled; omission undermines the credibility of the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts will find agency action unlawful if based on faulty, biased, or unsupported factual premises
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency action is unlawful if it 'relies on faulty or biased data,' 'fails to appropriately consider countervailing evidence,' or 'rests upon a factual premise that is unsupported by substantial evidence.' (citing Flyers Rights, Tex. Oil & Gas, New Orleans v. SEC, and other cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For defensible agency decisions, the administrative record must be accurate, unbiased, consider contrary evidence, and be supported by substantial evidence. Reliance on a flawed report that contradicts the weight of scientific evidence risks vacatur as arbitrary and capricious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deference to agency expertise requires substantial evidence and reasoned decisionmaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts defer to agency expertise only when the decision is 'supported by substantial evidence in the record and reached by reasoned decisionmaking, including an examination of the relevant data and a reasoned explanation supported by a stated connection between the facts found and the choice made.' If the agency 'simply has not exercised its expertise' or failed to engage with prior findings, deference is not warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must demonstrate engagement with existing scientific findings, analyze relevant data, and provide reasoned explanations; failure to do so removes Chevron-type deference and increases likelihood of reversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors indicating a product is ISI/HISA (establishing significant precedent, economic impact, controversial nature, cross-Agency implications, innovative approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA Peer Review Handbook lists factors for ISI including that the product '[e]stablishes a significant precedent;' is 'likely to adversely affect in a material way the economy; a sector of the economy; ... jobs; the environment; public health or safety; or state, tribal or local governments or communities;' '[a]ddresses significant controversial issues;' has 'significant cross-Agency/interagency implications;' and 'considers an innovative approach for a previously defined problem/process/methodology.' HISA adds criteria for high dollar impacts or novelty/controversy/interagency interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When these factors are present, agencies should treat the product as ISI or HISA and apply heightened review, external panels, and public participation. Ignoring these indicators and treating the product as routine is inconsistent with EPA guidance.
